title: Redwood demo - Data handling & retention controls (Horizon Payments)
participants_header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (CTO, Horizon), Lena Ortiz (Head of Security), Tom Wu (SRE), Rachel Gomez (Product)
summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood data handling features: request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII detection, retention controls, KMS integrations, and Private/VPC considerations. Customer asked about retention policies, audit logs, and demo of toggles in Console + API. Action items: share SOC2 and security whitepaper, provide retention config examples and a short pilot proposal + pricing sheet.
topics: Request storage toggles (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
Demo of Redwood Console + API + Optimize recommendations
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Rivera: hey everyone thanks for joining uh we have about 40 minutes, i'll kick off — i'm alex from redwood, that's priya on the call who will run the demo.
[00:12] Mark Chen: cool thanks alex, excited to see the data handling stuff, this is top of mind for us.
[00:18] Priya Malhotra: great, quick agenda, high level overview, security/controls, live demo of console toggles and api flags, then q/a and next steps. will try to keep it tight.
[00:30] Lena Ortiz: just a reminder i'm going to ask a lot of security-y questions, SSO, auditability, and retention.
[00:38] Alex Rivera: totally expected, please stop us any time. quick qualification — mark, tom — can you remind us of your current flow? are you hitting openai or self-hosted right now?
[00:50] Mark Chen: we use a mix — prod uses a managed provider but we also run some inference on prem for certain flows. code name for it is legacy-infer, not ideal. mostly we call external endpoints for non-PII stuff.
[01:05] Tom Wu: and we're very strict on PII, so anything customer-identifying has to either be redacted client-side or not stored. we need per-route retention policies.
[01:15] Alex Rivera: great, that maps to the areas we'll demo: per-route request storage toggles, automatic redaction, and encryption at rest with customer KMS.
[01:24] Priya Malhotra: starting demo — i'm in the redwood console now, Projects > Horizon-payments demo org, here's Routes. you can see a toggle for "Store requests" on each route. if you flip it off for a route requests won't be persisted to our storage. note: request logs used for debugging and quality monitoring will be disabled.
[01:45] Rachel Gomez: is that toggle per environment? like prod and staging separate?
[01:51] Priya Malhotra: yep per route per environment, and you can bulk edit via the API. i'll show the api flag in a sec.
[02:00] [02:00] Jordan Lee: (jumping in) small note: when store requests is off we still collect minimal telemetry for billing/usage — token counts and durations but not the payload.
[02:12] Lena Ortiz: okay that's good, are those token counts reversible for audits? i.e., do you keep any context or hashed keys?
[02:20] Priya Malhotra: token counts are aggregated, not tied to the raw prompt. we can provide per-request metadata like timestamp, model, latency, but not the raw content.
[02:31] [02:31] Mark Chen: how about redaction? we have a lot of card numbers and ssn like things in support transcripts, we need automatic masking.
[02:40] Priya Malhotra: we have built-in PII detection + redaction pipelines — it's rule-based plus ML heuristics. you can configure aggressive redaction where any detected entity is replaced with [REDACTED] in logs and retained payloads. here's the settings screen.
[02:58] Alex Rivera: note — detection isn't perfect; we recommend client-side tokenization and redaction for ultra-sensitive flows, but the console-level redaction prevents most leakage.
[03:10] Tom Wu: and is the redaction applied before data leaves our network? we want to avoid sending raw PII to any external network.
[03:18] Priya Malhotra: on our Private deployment it can be configured so redaction happens in your VPC before it hits the control plane. in hosted mode redaction occurs in our processing pipeline; if you need, we also offer a pre-ingest lambda hook for customer-side sanitization.
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: can you walk through KMS integration — we use AWS KMS and are evaluating HSM for keys.
[03:40] Jordan Lee: yes we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS out of the box; for HSM we integrate via customer-managed key providers and can provide a bring-your-own-hsm option for Private. keys are used for encrypting stored payloads and audit logs.
[03:58] [03:58] Mark Chen: does that include KV cache encryption? we do not want cached prefixes to be readable by anyone.
[04:05] Priya Malhotra: KV cache is encrypted at rest and can be configured to use your KMS; caching can also be disabled per route if you don't want any server-side caching.
[04:16] Alex Rivera: quick pause for timeline/business — what's your target timeline for a pilot?
[04:22] Mark Chen: if pricing makes sense we'd like to pilot prod flows within 4 weeks; security needs time to review though.
[04:28] Alex Rivera: good, we'll include a pilot proposal.
[04:32] [04:32] Priya Malhotra: back to demo — now showing API example: POST /v1/requests?store=false and header x-redwood-retention: short=7d; you can set retention windows per request or route. here's a sample curl.
[04:49] Rachel Gomez: can we set retention by data classification? e.g., route A stores 30d for non-PII, but PII auto-redacted and not stored.
[04:56] Priya Malhotra: yes you can chain rules — route-level defaults, then per-request override, plus content-classification triggers that force immediate redact or drop.
[05:06] [05:06] Lena Ortiz: audit logs — we need immutable trails for all admin changes, who toggled store requests, who accessed logs. how long are these retained?
[05:15] Jordan Lee: audit logs are stored in a separate append-only log, retention configurable up to 7 years for Private; hosted has a default retention of 1 year but we can negotiate longer with enterprise contracts. logs include actor, timestamp, changed field, and old/new values.
[05:34] Mark Chen: are audit logs exportable to our SIEM? we use Splunk.
[05:38] Priya Malhotra: yes you can stream audit events to Splunk/Datadog via syslog or direct APIs; we also have a webhook connector.
[05:46] [05:46] Tom Wu: another technical — performance — if we enable aggressive redaction and per-request encryption, will that add latency?
[05:55] Priya Malhotra: there is a small penalty, typically 10-30ms per request for redaction and another 5-15ms for envelope encryption depending on key latency. our Optimize recommendations will show tradeoffs and suggest batching where acceptable.
[06:12] Alex Rivera: to add, for high-throughput low-latency we often recommend Dedicated capacity with hardware-backed KMS proximity — that reduces KMS roundtrip time.
[06:23] Mark Chen: cost vs latency is always the dance; curious about Redwood Optimize — can it automatically recommend quantization or batching per route?
[06:31] Priya Malhotra: yes Redwood Optimize analyzes token distributions and latency targets and will suggest quant profiles, batching windows, and cache policies. the Optimize UI shows expected unit cost impact and estimated latency changes.
[06:43] [06:43] Jordan Lee: small transcription glitch: sometimes the console shows "optima" in the UI during early rollouts — it's the same thing.
[06:50] Lena Ortiz: what about deletion requests from customers (subject access requests)? we need a legal hold/erase workflow per user id.
[06:59] Priya Malhotra: we provide APIs to query and delete by customer id; for hosted offerings we process deletes within SLA windows and can provide proof via audit logs. for Private you control deletion directly.
[07:12] Mark Chen: okay good. any certifications? SOC2 primarily, ISO next?
[07:18] Alex Rivera: we are SOC2 Type II and are pursuing ISO27001; i'll send the attestation pack.
[07:25] [07:25] Rachel Gomez: can we see an example of the redact pipeline in the console?
[07:29] Priya Malhotra: sure showing redact rules: regex-based rules for CC, SSN, email, plus ml detectors. you can preview redaction on sample payloads to validate.
[07:41] [07:41] Mark Chen: these ML detectors — can we tune false positives? some product copy has weird patterns that trigger.
[07:48] Jordan Lee: yes you can supply allowlists and custom patterns; we ship a tunable sensitivity slider for each detector.
[07:56] Tom Wu: how are these rules versioned? we need reproducible audit trails for model evals.
[08:03] Priya Malhotra: rules and detectors are versioned; changes create a new rule-set id and changelog entry that shows who changed it and when.
[08:12] [08:12] Mark Chen: any limits on retention windows? can we do 30 days, 90 days, perpetual?
[08:19] Alex Rivera: hosted default up to 1 year but can extend contractually; Dedicated and Private can support custom windows including infinite retention if required by contract.
[08:29] Lena Ortiz: for compliance we want separation of duties — can we restrict who toggles store requests? role based access?
[08:36] Jordan Lee: yes RBAC with SSO (SAML/OIDC), we integrate with Okta, Azure AD — you can create granular roles (route-admin, security-admin, auditor).
[08:49] [08:49] Priya Malhotra: now demoing live API call. typing cURL... curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/requests -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'x-redwood-retention: short=7d' -d '{"prompt":"support ticket with cc 4111-..."}' and you can see response: request accepted, stored=false, id=xxxx.
[09:12] Mark Chen: side question: does redaction happen before the model sees the prompt or after? we have some safety flows where model should see redacted material only.
[09:21] Priya Malhotra: redaction by default is applied to logs/storage; you can opt-in to pipeline redaction which removes PII before model input — that requires model-aware tokenization but we support it.
[09:33] [09:33] Rachel Gomez: can we run test jobs to measure latency impact? we'd want this on our staging with sample traffic.
[09:40] Alex Rivera: yes we'll set up a 2-week pilot in your staging env; SEs will assist with load scripts and suggested configs.
[09:48] Lena Ortiz: i want to schedule a security review with our team — can you share threat models and pen-test results?
[09:54] Jordan Lee: we'll send the security pack and summarize pen test scope; pen-test reports are available under NDA — we'll include that in the folder.
[10:03] [10:03] Tom Wu: what's the rollback story if we misconfigure retention and accidentally store data?
[10:09] Priya Malhotra: admins can revoke access, request deletion, and we have an incident workflow; for hosted environments we help execute data scrubs under enterprise contracts and provide audit evidence.
[10:21] Mark Chen: sounds reasonable. any competitor callouts we should be aware of? we've also looked at Bedrock and a few smaller vendors.
[10:29] Alex Rivera: competitors mentioned — OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Cohere — we often differentiate on observability and per-route economics.
[10:38] [10:38] Priya Malhotra: quick perf note: if you need sub-50ms p95 for auth token checks, we typically recommend Dedicated + local KMS.
[10:46] Rachel Gomez: ok let's talk next steps and ownership.
[10:50] Alex Rivera: recap and next steps: i'll send SOC2 and security whitepaper, priya and jordan will send retention config examples and a pilot proposal + pricing. we'll also schedule a security deep-dive with lena next week.
[11:05] Mark Chen: good. l'll share internal contact for procurement and compliance.
[11:09] Lena Ortiz: thanks, and please include a sample SLA for audit log retention and export.
[11:14] Alex Rivera: will do. thanks everyone.
[11:18] [11:18] Priya Malhotra: (closing) sharing links in chat: security pack (link), pilot proposal template (link), pricing sheet (link) — we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[11:30] Speaker 1: thanks all bye.
[11:33] Alex Rivera: bye
